- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 38.18 → 36.98 in Example 1), then overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Model underreacts to sustained downward trends in history (e.g., 36.62 → 33.77 in Example 1), failing to adjust mean reversion.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in responding to true price drops, especially when history includes recent low points.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the 30d forecast, particularly when history includes high volatility or recent spikes.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the true mean reversion behavior — overestimating recovery after sharp declines.
- When history includes a recent spike followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect upward, then undercorrect downward.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, especially when true outcomes show sharp upward moves.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days of the 30d window, then gradually adjust — but often too late to capture true trend reversal.
